result: ROCK inhibition leads to ectopic SOX2 expression in outside cells and increases outside cells with mixed lineage (CDX2+/SOX2+). Embryos treated with ROCK inhibitor (ROCKi) for 24 hours showed SOX2 expression in outside cells, which normally express only CDX2, and a substantial proportion of outside cells coexpressed both CDX2 and SOX2.
evaluation: Claims C6-C7 and C86-C88 provide converging experimental evidence from ROCKi treatment experiments showing ectopic SOX2 in outside cells and mixed lineage marker expression. The data includes proper controls (DMSO), demonstrates effective ROCK inhibition (mislocalized PARD6B/CDH1), and quantifies the phenotype across multiple embryos with statistical significance.

result: Constitutively active nuclear YAP1 (YAP1CA) is sufficient to repress SOX2 expression in inner cell mass cells. Overexpression of YAP1CA, which remains constitutively nuclear due to S112A mutation, led to a conspicuous decrease in SOX2-positive inside cells compared to non-injected controls.
evaluation: Claims C8, C72, and C89-C91 demonstrate that nuclear YAP1 represses Sox2 through gain-of-function experiments. The YAP1CA construct is properly validated (constitutively nuclear localization confirmed), includes appropriate controls (non-injected cells), and shows clear phenotypic effects on SOX2 expression in inside cells.

result: LATS2 overexpression drives cells to inside position and induces SOX2 expression regardless of cell position. Almost all Lats2-overexpressing cells localized to the inner cell mass by blastocyst stage, with SOX2 detected in all inside Lats2-overexpressing cells and even in rare outside Lats2-overexpressing cells. This repositioning occurs starting around the 32-cell stage.
evaluation: Claims C9-C11, C13, and C92-C95 provide comprehensive temporal and spatial analysis of Lats2 overexpression effects. The data includes proper controls (GFP-only injected cells), time-course analysis showing timing of effects, statistical analysis (chi-squared tests), and demonstrates both cell-autonomous effects and position-independent SOX2 induction.

result: LATS2 promotes inside cell positioning by regulating YAP1 and WWTR1 activities. Co-overexpression of constitutively active YAP1 (Yap1CA) with Lats2 partially rescued the inside positioning phenotype, reduced cell death (TUNEL-positive cells), and increased the proportion of Lats2-overexpressing cells remaining in outside positions.
evaluation: Claims C12 and C96-C100 demonstrate epistasis through rescue experiments. The Yap1CA co-overexpression reverses both the positioning and survival phenotypes of Lats2 overexpression, with statistical support (chi-squared tests) and proper controls, establishing that LATS2 acts through YAP1/WWTR1.

result: LATS2-mediated cell positioning and survival occur independently of Sox2. Lats2-overexpressing cells were equally likely to occupy inside positions in both wild-type and Sox2 maternal/zygotic null embryos, and deletion of Sox2 did not rescue survival of cells with elevated HIPPO signaling.
evaluation: Claims C14-C15, C44, C52, and C101-C102 use genetic deletion of Sox2 to test its requirement for LATS2-mediated effects. The experiments show no significant differences in cell positioning between genotypes (proper statistical tests), demonstrating that Sox2 is dispensable for LATS2's effects on cell positioning and survival.

result: LATS2 overexpression antagonizes apical localization of aPKCz and PARD6B in outside cells. At 16-32 cell stages, most Lats2-overexpressing outside cells lacked detectable aPKCz and PARD6B at the apical membrane, while these proteins were properly localized in control cells.
evaluation: Claims C16-C17 and C103 demonstrate a specific effect of LATS2 on apical domain components through immunofluorescence analysis. The data includes proper controls (GFP-injected and non-injected cells), appropriate developmental timing, and quantification showing statistical significance, providing a mechanistic link between LATS2 and cell positioning.

result: Other polarity markers remain properly localized in Lats2-overexpressing outside cells. CDH1 was restricted to basolateral membranes, while filamentous Actin and phospho-ERM were properly localized to apical domains in both Lats2-overexpressing and control outside cells at 16-32 cell stages.
evaluation: Claims C18 and C104-C106 demonstrate specificity of LATS2's effects on polarity by showing that not all polarity markers are disrupted. The data from multiple markers (CDH1, F-actin, pERM) with proper localization indicates selective disruption of aPKC/PARD6B rather than complete loss of polarity.

result: Sox2 expression is more sensitive than Cdx2 to Wwtr1/Yap1 dosage, creating cells with mixed lineage at intermediate gene doses. With decreasing wild-type alleles of Wwtr1 and Yap1, embryos showed progressively more ectopic SOX2 in outside cells, while CDX2 expression persisted at reduced levels in intermediate genotypes but was severely reduced only in complete knockouts.
evaluation: Claims C19-C22 and C107-C110 use a genetic dosage series to demonstrate differential sensitivity of Sox2 vs Cdx2 to YAP1/WWTR1 activity. The data shows graded phenotypes correlating with gene dosage, proper controls (wild-type and heterozygous embryos), and statistical analysis, revealing that intermediate doses produce mixed-lineage cells expressing both markers.

result: Loss of Wwtr1 and Yap1 leads to increased inside cells, decreased outside cells, and ectopic SOX2 expression in outside cells. Embryos with one or fewer wild-type alleles showed increased inside/outside cell ratios, with the remaining outside cells exhibiting ectopic SOX2 expression, demonstrating that WWTR1/YAP1 repress inner cell mass fate downstream of LATS kinases.
evaluation: Claims C23, C25-C26, and C111-C114 provide loss-of-function genetic evidence complementing the overexpression studies. The data includes quantification of cell populations across multiple genotypes with statistical analysis (student's t-tests), showing dose-dependent effects on both cell positioning and Sox2 expression.

result: WWTR1 is a more potent repressor of Sox2 than YAP1 at E3.75. Embryos with a single wild-type allele of Wwtr1 had significantly fewer outside cells with ectopic SOX2 compared to embryos with a single wild-type allele of Yap1, and the percentage of outside cells with ectopic SOX2 increased progressively with decreasing gene dosage.
evaluation: Claims C27 and C115-C118 compare the relative contributions of WWTR1 vs YAP1 through analysis of different heterozygous combinations. The data shows statistically significant differences between Wwtr1 and Yap1 single heterozygotes, with proper quantification and controls, revealing differential potency of the two paralogs.

result: Loss of Wwtr1/Yap1 disrupts apical domain formation while preserving some polarity markers. Embryos with one or fewer doses of Wwtr1/Yap1 showed greatly reduced aPKC at apical membranes and disorganized ZO-1, but CDH1 and pERM remained correctly localized, indicating that WWTR1/YAP1 are crucial for apical domain formation while some apicobasal polarity is maintained.
evaluation: Claims C28, C30-C31, and C120-C122 characterize the polarity defects in Wwtr1/Yap1 mutants through analysis of multiple markers. The data shows selective disruption of specific apical components (aPKC, ZO-1) while others remain properly localized (CDH1, pERM), providing mechanistic insight into how YAP1/WWTR1 regulate cell positioning.

result: YAP1/WWTR1 are key components that repress Sox2 expression in outside cells through antagonizing apical localization of Par complex components PARD6B and aPKC, establishing a negative feedback loop between HIPPO and Par complex components that ensures robust lineage segregation.
evaluation: Claims C33-C34, C55, C58-C59 synthesize the major findings into a coherent model. The conclusion is supported by converging evidence from multiple experimental approaches (ROCK inhibition, YAP1CA overexpression, LATS2 overexpression, genetic deletion) showing consistent effects on Sox2 expression and Par complex localization.

result: Intermediate YAP1/WWTR1 activity creates conflicted cell fate with coexpression of Sox2 and Cdx2. Inside cells could initially possess intermediate doses of active YAP1/WWTR1 during early blastocyst formation, consistent with initial CDX2 detection in inside cells where SOX2 is also expressed.
evaluation: Claims C35-C36, C56, and C78 propose a model for how differential sensitivity to YAP1/WWTR1 creates transient mixed-lineage states. The model is supported by the dosage series data showing coexpression at intermediate levels and is consistent with published observations of CDX2 in inside cells during blastocyst formation.

result: HIPPO signaling ensures robust developmental transitions by repositioning SOX2-expressing cells to inside positions around the 32-cell stage, coinciding with loss of cell fate plasticity and formation of mature tight junctions. This repositioning occurs independent of HIPPO's role in regulating Sox2 expression.
evaluation: Claims C37-C39 and C57 integrate the temporal findings with the mechanistic insights. The timing of HIPPO-induced internalization (32-cell stage) is supported by the time-course data (C13), and the independence from Sox2 regulation is demonstrated by the genetic experiments (C14-C15). The correlation with tight junction formation is supported by citations.

result: HIPPO signaling interferes with trophectoderm epithelialization and engages in negative feedback with cell polarity components. Lats2-overexpressing outside cells initially possess hallmarks of apicobasal polarization, but aPKC and PARD6B fail to properly localize, leading to eventual depolarization and internalization.
evaluation: Claims C40-C41 and C85 propose a feedback mechanism based on the observation that HIPPO disrupts specific polarity components (C16-C17) while others remain intact (C18). The model is supported by the temporal analysis showing initial polarization followed by selective loss of aPKC/PARD6B, though the feedback mechanism itself is somewhat speculative.

result: A small proportion of cells with conflicted fate undergo apoptosis downstream of YAP1/WWTR1. Cell lethality due to elevated HIPPO can be rescued by increasing nuclear YAP1 levels, suggesting YAP1 provides a pro-survival signal to trophectoderm cells. Apoptosis increases after the 32-cell stage, with extensive TUNEL staining in embryos lacking Wwtr1/Yap1.
evaluation: Claims C42-C43, C80-C81, and C119 demonstrate cell death as one mechanism for eliminating conflicted cells. The data includes TUNEL assays showing increased apoptosis in both Lats2-overexpressing embryos and Wwtr1/Yap1 mutants, and rescue experiments showing Yap1CA reduces cell death, with proper controls and statistical analysis.

result: Cells with elevated HIPPO signaling drive their own internalization, consistent with Tead4 knockdown causing internalization. However, YAP1/WWTR1 loss of function leads to loss of apical PARD6B/aPKC while Tead4 loss preserves the apical domain, suggesting YAP1/WWTR1 could partner with proteins other than TEAD4 (possibly TEAD1) to regulate apical domain formation.
evaluation: Claims C45-C49 compare the current findings with published Tead4 studies to identify mechanistic differences. The observation that Yap1/Wwtr1 and Tead4 loss-of-function have different effects on the apical domain (C47) is well-supported by the data, and the speculation about alternative TEAD partners is reasonable given the phenotypic differences, though it requires further testing.

result: PARD6B/aPKC are essential for outside cell positioning, and their loss would eventually lead to cell depolarization, which could influence processes governing inside cell allocation such as oriented cleavage, cell contractility, or apical constriction.
evaluation: Claims C50-C51 connect the observed loss of aPKC/PARD6B to potential downstream mechanisms affecting cell positioning. The essential role of PARD6B/aPKC is supported by multiple citations, and the proposed mechanisms are reasonable inferences based on established roles of these proteins, though the specific mechanisms remain to be tested.

result: SOX2 is associated with future pluripotent state but does not alone contribute to all aspects of pluripotency such as inside positioning. This interpretation is consistent with observations that SOX2 dwells longer in nuclei of four-cell stage embryos destined for inner cell mass, though SOX2 activity has been proposed to bias inner cell mass fate.
evaluation: Claims C53-C54 and C82 interpret the Sox2 deletion results (C14-C15, C52) in the context of published observations. The conclusion that Sox2 is dispensable for positioning is directly supported by the genetic experiments, and the discussion of SOX2's association with pluripotency without controlling all aspects is a reasonable interpretation of the data.

result: Background context on early embryo lineage specification: SOX2 is the first marker of pluripotency expressed specifically in inside cells at the 16-cell stage, while CDX2 is expressed in outer cells. Sox2 is restricted to inside cells by a Cdx2-independent mechanism, differing from Oct4 and Nanog which are restricted by CDX2. Sox2 and Cdx2 are regulated in parallel, and at E3.25, SOX2 and CDX2 are normally mutually exclusive.
evaluation: These claims (C1-C3, C32, C60-C68, C75-C77) establish the background context for the study through citations to published literature. The claims are well-supported by multiple references and provide the foundation for understanding why the current study focuses on Sox2 regulation. These are primarily literature-based claims that set up the research questions.

result: Background on HIPPO pathway regulation: HIPPO pathway kinases LATS1/2 become active in inside cells and antagonize YAP1/WWTR1/TEAD4 activity. ROCK kinases act upstream of Cdx2, ROCK activity is required for nuclear YAP1 localization, and Tead4 is required to repress Sox2 in trophectoderm. LATS2 inactivates YAP1/WWTR1 by phosphorylation causing cytoplasmic retention.
evaluation: Claims C4-C5, C69-C71, C73-C74 provide background on HIPPO pathway components and their known roles, supported by extensive citations. These establish the rationale for investigating YAP1/WWTR1 in Sox2 regulation and provide the mechanistic framework for interpreting the experimental results.

result: Background on cell positioning mechanisms: Trophectoderm cell fate has been proposed to be determined by apically localized membrane components that maintain outside cell position. The apical membrane components aPKC and PARD6B are required for maintaining outside cell position and trophectoderm fate.
evaluation: Claims C83-C84 provide background on the role of apical polarity components in cell positioning, supported by multiple citations. This background is essential for understanding the significance of the findings that LATS2/YAP1/WWTR1 regulate aPKC/PARD6B localization.
